sentences.text: This dinosaur weighed approximately one tonne and stood about 1.5 to 2 meters tall at the hips.
It possessed an elongated skull that was broader towards the front.
Unique anatomical features include a sharp ridge on the supraoccipital, elongated frontal bones, a horseshoe-shaped atlas intercentrum, and a distinct ridge on the inner side of the ilium.
The holotype specimen of Leshansaurus was discovered in 2007.
Leshansaurus was named and described in 2009 by a team of Chinese paleontologists including Li Fei and Peng Guangzhao.
The name Leshansaurus qianweiensis honors the city of Leshan and the county of Qianwei in Sichuan, China, where the fossils were found.
Leshansaurus fossils were found in the Shangshaximiao Formation, a geological layer known for its rich dinosaur fossil content.
While originally placed in Sinraptoridae, Leshansaurus may actually belong to the family Megalosauridae.
Leshansaurus is classified within the family Megalosauridae.
A 2012 analysis by Matthew Carrano placed Leshansaurus in the subfamily Afrovenatorinae as a sister species to Piveteausaurus.
Leshansaurus lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now China.
Leshansaurus lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic in Asia.
Leshansaurus lived between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian and Callovian stages.
It is debated whether Leshansaurus belongs to the carnosaurian group Sinraptoridae or the family Megalosauridae.
